overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the complaint about the Dec. 18, 2019 minutes or their website posting, citing the Board's revision, and issued only cautions and a reminder on the unprompted notice concerns.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Dec. 18, 2019 minutes wrongly said a Land Court case was filed by residents rather than the realty trust; the Board had already revised them.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, at the time the complaint was filed with our office, the Board had already revised the minutes at issue and the complaint filed with our office “has no dispute with the new minutes.”

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the original Dec. 18, 2019 minutes be removed from the town website, where both original and amended versions were posted.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their minutes to a website.

allegations.summary: Unprompted by the complaint, the AG reviewed the Dec. 18, 2019 notice's executive session purpose, which cited 'ongoing litigation' without naming the case.
allegations.key_passage: A public body should include the specific case name of the litigation matter it plans to discuss unless doing so would compromise the Board’s litigating position.

allegations.summary: Unprompted by the complaint, the AG found the notice topic 'ongoing litigation' too vague and reminded the Board to name litigation matters in notices.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, the topic “ongoing litigation” would not have been sufficiently specific even for discussion in open session.
